candidate.title: TruSeq™ PCR Free
candidate.scope: The assigned single TruSeq PCR Free product-preparation schematic, from double-stranded DNA to an indexed, adapter-ligated DNA library ready for cluster generation. No distinct method alternatives are depicted. The PCR Free title and drawn route identify a library preparation without a depicted library-PCR stage; cluster generation and sequencing are downstream of the illustrated endpoint. The starting DNA's organism, genomic or other origin, and cell provenance are not specified.

states.label: Double-stranded DNA
features: Input DNA is drawn as two long blue strands; no biological specimen or sequence-specific target is identified.

evidence.locator: Top: Double-stranded DNA label and long paired blue lines

states.label: Fractionated, size-selected DNA fragments
features: Shorter paired blue DNA strands after the first downward arrow; ends have not yet undergone the depicted repair and phosphorylation.

evidence.locator: Short paired strands below Fractionate / Size select

states.label: End-repaired, phosphorylated DNA fragments
features: Duplex strands terminate at aligned ends, with short purple terminal segments and P symbols on opposite strand termini.
The P symbols are interpreted as terminal phosphate groups because the preceding caption explicitly says Phosphorylate; numerical strand polarity is not labelled.

evidence.locator: Duplex below End repair / Phosphorylate: purple terminal segments and circled P symbols
End repair / Phosphorylate caption and P symbols on the resulting duplex
evidence.rationale: The phosphorylation caption identifies the meaning of P; the extraction retains the terminal positions shown without assigning unprinted strand-polarity numbers.

states.label: A-overhang DNA fragments
features: End-repaired DNA now carries a protruding A at the upper-right and lower-left strand termini; P symbols remain on the opposite termini.

evidence.locator: Central duplex below A-overhang: purple A at each protruding end and opposite P marks

states.label: Indexed forked adapters with T termini
features: Two oppositely oriented forked adapter drawings bear P5, P7 and Index labels.
T and P symbols mark the duplex-facing adapter termini; the two drawings supply the two insert ends rather than alternative workflows.

evidence.locator: Below plus sign: left and right forked adapters with T, P, P5, P7 and Index labels

states.label: A-overhang DNA combined with adapters
features: Reaction assembly represented by the plus sign linking A-overhang DNA and the two oriented adapters before the ligation arrow; covalent attachment is represented by the subsequent operation.

evidence.locator: Add Adapters region: A-overhang duplex, plus sign and forked adapters above Adapter ligation arrow
evidence.rationale: The Add Adapters caption and explicit plus sign establish a combined reaction input; the next arrow labelled Adapter ligation leads to attached adapters. This boundary separates reagent addition from covalent ligation without inventing a further chemical transformation.

states.label: Product ready for cluster generation
features: A central double-stranded DNA insert is joined to forked adapter structures at both ends.
P5, P7 and Index labels are retained beside the terminal adapter arms.
The physical readout carrier is the prepared DNA insert linked to adapter sequences; actual clusters, reads and analysis are not drawn.

evidence.locator: Bottom: adapter-flanked blue duplex, P5/P7/Index labels, and Product ready for cluster generation caption
Blue duplex retained through the preparation route and final Product ready for cluster generation label
evidence.rationale: The retained central DNA insert is the material carrying input-derived sequence into the cluster-generation interface. Sequencing reads themselves are outside the drawn route.

operations.label: Fractionate / Size select
operations.description: The input double-stranded DNA is reduced to shorter fragments and a size-selected fragment population is retained. The single illustrated transition combines these two captioned actions without specifying their internal execution.
operations.information_effect: The library precursor represents retained fragments of the starting DNA; size selection restricts the fragment population, without a depicted sequence-specific biological selection.

evidence.locator: First downward arrow: long input strands to shorter strands; Fractionate / Size select caption
Fractionate / Size select caption and long-to-short DNA transition
evidence.rationale: Retaining size-selected pieces of the input means that the precursor library represents the retained fragment population. The schematic supplies no sequence-specific enrichment or completeness claim.

operations.label: End repair / Phosphorylate
operations.description: Fragment termini are repaired to the aligned duplex ends shown and acquire the depicted terminal phosphate marks; short purple segments appear at two strand ends.
operations.mechanism: End repair and phosphorylation are named; no enzyme or individual repair reaction is specified.
operations.information_effect: Changes end chemistry for the following adapter-preparation steps while retaining the DNA-fragment carrier.

evidence.locator: Second downward arrow and End repair / Phosphorylate caption, ending at aligned P-marked duplex

operations.label: A-overhang
operations.description: The repaired, phosphorylated DNA gains protruding terminal A residues on opposite strand ends, while the P-marked ends are retained.
operations.mechanism: Addition of the depicted A overhangs; no enzyme is identified.
operations.information_effect: Creates A-bearing DNA termini at the future DNA-insert/adapter interface; the following adapter drawings have T-bearing termini.

evidence.locator: Third downward arrow labelled A-overhang, from repaired duplex to A-terminated duplex
A-overhang duplex followed by T-labelled forked adapters below the plus sign

operations.label: Add Adapters
operations.description: The A-overhang DNA and the T-bearing, indexed forked adapters are combined as inputs for ligation. The left and right adapter drawings correspond to attachment at the two ends of one insert, with no separate processing branch or pooling shown.
operations.mechanism: Reagent addition, indicated by the plus sign; attachment is represented by the next ligation operation.
operations.information_effect: Introduces the Index-labelled and P5/P7-bearing material that will become physically associated with each retained DNA insert.

evidence.locator: Add Adapters caption, A-overhang duplex, plus sign and pair of oppositely oriented adapters

operations.label: Adapter ligation
operations.description: Adapters are joined at both ends of the A-overhang DNA, producing the continuous adapter-flanked duplex shown at the bottom and labelled ready for cluster generation.
operations.mechanism: The caption identifies ligation, and the output shows adapters attached at both ends of the insert. The preceding inputs bear A and T overhang labels and terminal P marks; no enzyme identity is specified.
operations.information_effect: The input-derived DNA fragment remains the biological sequence carrier and becomes physically linked to adapter-derived Index and P5/P7 elements. The product is an interface to cluster generation; downstream insert reads would represent retained DNA fragments. The drawing supplies no read-level measurement, cell-identity association or assertion of complete input coverage.

evidence.locator: Adapter ligation caption and downward arrow to final insert with adapters at both ends
Adapter ligation output: central blue DNA insert connected to P5/P7/Index-labelled arms; Product ready for cluster generation caption
evidence.rationale: The continuous central insert carries the retained input DNA sequence, while the attached labelled adapter arms provide the depicted cluster-generation interface and index association. Thus downstream insert sequence would describe retained DNA fragments. The schematic does not establish index design, cell identity, quantitative measurement or complete input coverage.

method_scopes.rationale: The card and image title identify a single product-preparation target. All five local operations belong to its one connected route. The paired adapter icons supply opposite insert ends and do not identify method alternatives. Applicability is resolved for this schematic, without claiming a complete protocol or an implementation version beyond the title. No primary-paper association is supplied or required by the card.

checks.rationale: Independently inspected the supplied PNG and catalogue card and checked every supplied review target. The candidate represents all five captioned transformations, all material interfaces, the depicted terminal modifications, the two adapter orientations and the final cluster-generation interface. The original DNA remains the insert carrier through fragmentation and end modification; indexed adapter material joins it at both ends. The plus sign supports a joint addition operation, rather than separate biological branches. No compartment, attachment state, alternative workflow or depicted output is lost. Biological origin, index design and downstream measurements are appropriately left unspecified. The catalogue supplies no publications and explicitly requires no paper match; an empty paper_matches list and no paper-supported corrections are appropriate. No consequential unsupported claim, missing depicted transformation or unresolved source conflict was found at this schematic's scope.
